note:
Two curates sharing 5 Park Terrace (#245) on the 1891 return, with a cook and a housemaid, transcribed by A. Hagues. None of the four was in the record, and 5 Park Terrace held only 1921, so 1891 is free.

Leonard J W Thomson, 27, is curate of St Margaret's; Edward P Anderson, 27, returned as a lodger, is curate of St Thomas's and was born in Glasgow. Two curates of the same age keeping house together reads as shared clergy lodgings rather than a family household, and neither is joined to the other. Both had gone by 1894, when Wright's Directory prints Job E. Sanby of the Midland Lace Company at number 5; curates moved on quickly, so this is unsurprising.

The head's surname is entered as transcribed, Thomson without the p. Ages are as the enumerator wrote them, so a birth year worked back from one may be a year out either way.
source: 1891 census, 5 Park Terrace, transcribed by A. Hagues. Directory evidence: Wright's Directory of Nottingham 1894-95, page 107 (Leicester Special Collections id 164613).
